entities.label: Text
entities.summary:
Collection of short stories by Arthur Conan Doyle Created by Arthur Conan Doyle.

The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes is a seminal work in the detective fiction genre, offering a unique blend of intellectual curiosity and social commentary. First published in 1892, the collection of 12 short stories revolutionized the genre with its emphasis on reason, science, and observation.

Through the character of Sherlock Holmes, Doyle critiqued societal norms and challenged prevailing attitudes towards crime and justice. The stories' exploration of themes such as identity, morality, and the human condition continues to captivate readers today.

The impact of The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes extends beyond literary circles; its influence can be seen in popular culture, from film adaptations to television shows. The character of Sherlock Holmes has become an iconic figure, symbolizing intelligence, wit, and analytical thinking.

One of the most striking aspects of this collection is its ability to transcend time and geography, speaking to readers across cultures and continents.

The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes remains a testament to Doyle's mastery of storytelling, offering a glimpse into the intellectual and social currents of late 19th-century England.

Their legacy is studied through the lens of historical causation.", "summary": "The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes is a collection of twelve short stories by Sir Arthur Conan Doyle (1859–1930), first published in the Strand Magazine (July 1891 – June 1892) and collected in book form by George Newnes Ltd in October 1892. The twelve stories — 'A Scandal in Bohemia', 'The Red-Headed League', 'A Case of Identity', 'The Boscombe Valley Mystery', 'The Five Orange Pips', 'The Man with the Twisted Lip', 'The Adventure of the Blue Carbuncle', 'The Adventure of the Speckled Band', 'The Adventure of the Engineer's Thumb', 'The Adventure of the Noble Bachelor', 'The Adventure of the Beryl Coronet', and 'The Adventure of the Copper Beeches' — are among the most celebrated detective short stories in the English language, featuring the consulting detective Sherlock Holmes and his companion Dr. John H. Watson.

The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes was the first collection of the Holmes stories in the Strand Magazine, and the Strand's serialisation of the Holmes stories (1891–1927) is one of the landmark events in the history of mass-market magazine publishing and popular fiction. The Holmes stories in the Strand transformed Conan Doyle from a struggling novelist into the most popular fiction writer in Victorian and Edwardian England, and the demand for Holmes stories was so great that when Conan Doyle killed off Holmes in 'The Final Problem' (1893), public outcry forced him to revive the character (in 'The Adventure of the Empty House', 1903).

Sherlock Holmes — the consulting detective of 221B Baker Street, with his methods of scientific deduction, his violin, his cocaine habit (7% solution), his Moroccan tobacco, and his companion Watson — is the most famous fictional character in the English-speaking world and arguably the most widely recognised character in world literature.
